## Georgia O’Keeffe: Architecture

September 11, 2026 - January 3, 2027

[Facebook](https://www.facebook.com/sharer/sharer.php?u=https://dia.org/events/exhibitions/georgia-okeeffe-architecture) [Twitter](https://twitter.com/intent/tweet?text=https://dia.org/events/exhibitions/georgia-okeeffe-architecture) [?subject=Check%20this%20Dia%20collection%20link&body=https://dia.org/events/exhibitions/georgia-okeeffe-architecture](mailto:?subject=Check%20this%20Dia%20collection%20link&body=https://dia.org/events/exhibitions/georgia-okeeffe-architecture) [Link Copied](https://dia.org/events/exhibitions/georgia-okeeffe-architecture)

_Georgia O'Keeffe: Architecture_ is a groundbreaking exhibition that showcases approximately 35 architectural paintings created from the 1920s –1960s. O'Keeffe, a pioneer of modern art, celebrated the beauty and complexity of the built environments she inhabited through these remarkable works. Throughout her long career, the artist found inspiration through close observations of her surroundings, both natural and manmade. She returned many times to architectural subjects with the same powerful, abstract style used for her well-known depictions of flowers and desert landscapes.

O’Keeffe experimented with line, geometry, and color to develop her distinctive style. She painted the gleaming towers of new Manhattan skyscrapers, the broad sides of rural barns, and striking adobe homes of New Mexico. The buildings in the artist’s work, rich with personal meaning, encourage us to view our architectural surroundings with new eyes.

Questions about attending the exhibition or buying tickets? [Visit our Visitor Information page](https://dia.org/visit/faqs) to learn more.

Discover the stories behind Georgia O’Keeffe’s iconic paintings of New Mexico’s adobe architecture in this talk and demonstration with artist Joanna Keane Lopez. ### The Byron and Dorothy Gerson Lecture Series

Making Room: Georgia O'Keeffe and ArchitectureArchitecture runs through Georgia O'Keeffe's art from her earliest childhood sketches to her final works — not merely as subject matter, but as a way of seeing and understanding. In this talk, Dr. Cody Hartley, Director of the Georgia O’Keeffe Museum in Santa Fe, NM, traces how O'Keeffe lived with, altered, and built the spaces around her — shaping homes and studios that served her art-making, functioned as a form of self-expression, and framed her world for continual observation, study, and inspiration. Architecture was also fundamental to understanding new places as she traveled and relocated, from the barns of Lake George to the adobe walls of Northern New Mexico. And it situates her within a larger conversation in American art about how the nation's cities and landscapes might embody a distinct cultural identity — even as she claimed and built space, quite literally, for herself

### A House that Grew: O'Keeffe's Abiquiu Home

A House that Grew: O’Keeffe’s Abiquiu HomeNestled in the desert landscape of Abiquiú sits an unlikely an unlikely mid-century–modern masterpiece. With a discerning eye, Georgia O'Keeffe transformed a dilapidated 18th-century adobe house into an artist's sanctuary where she would go on to create some of her most iconic works. As her home and studio for nearly 40 years, it continually evolved — adapted again and again to her changing needs, tastes, and ways of living. This talk traces the architectural and design evolution of the property, exploring the alterations O'Keeffe made to its historic adobe architecture as well as the furnishings, objects, and mid-century-modern elements she brought into its rooms. Together, these changes reveal the home as an ongoing creative project – O’Keeffe’s largest work of art. Giustina Renzoni, Director of Historic Properties at the Georgia O'Keeffe Museum, will focus on O'Keeffe's life in New Mexico and in her houses. Renzoni will also discuss O'Keeffe's furnishings and design affinities.

### Gallery Talk and Tour: Georgia O'Keeffe Architecture

Georgia O'Keeffe: Architecture is a groundbreaking exhibition that showcases approximately 35 architectural paintings created from the 1920s –1960s. O'Keeffe, a pioneer of modern art, celebrated the beauty and complexity of the built environments she inhabited through these remarkable works. Throughout her long career, the artist found inspiration through close observations of her surroundings, both natural and manmade. She returned many times to architectural subjects with the same powerful, abstract style used for her well-known depictions of flowers and desert landscapes. O’Keeffe experimented with line, geometry, and color to develop her distinctive style. She painted the gleaming towers of new Manhattan skyscrapers, the broad sides of rural barns, and striking adobe homes of New Mexico. ### Member Preview: Georgia O'Keeffe: Architecture

Members see special exhibitions first! Register to reserve your spot to see Georgia O'Keeffe: Architecture.Georgia O’Keeffe’s paintings of architecture capture the dynamic characteristics of the built environment. The barns, skyscrapers, churches, and houses that she painted in her recognizable and abstracted style are filled with poignant personal meaning. Georgia O’Keeffe: Architecture will include approximately 35 paintings by the artist created during one of the most productive stages of her long career from the 1920s until the 1960s. The exhibition presents a fresh opportunity to consider O’Keeffe’s practice alongside timely notions of place making and identity. This is the first presentation of the full breadth of O’Keeffe’s architectural paintings and shows an unfamiliar side to a beloved artist who is renowned for her landscape and flower paintings. These works will challenge and inspire visitors to consider the beauty and complexity of the built environment that surrounds them.
